The Greeks, when they heard that Diogenes had been made sole ruler:
sent to them King Michael son of Constantine.
And this one took him to his mother:
who had been the wife of Diogenes.
And in Caesarea she was made a nun in a monastery.
And Caesar John, her uncle, was with her.
Diogenes, however, had gone up to the land of the Romans
and heard that this had happened.
He went up to the fortress of Duqiḥ.
And he gathered there two hundred thousand dinars,
and sent to the Sultan two emirs who had gone with him,

And he took the monastic habit of the monastic life.
And he stayed in Duqiḥ.
And he sent to Michael, saying:
that until now I have been fighting a fine struggle against the covenant of the Christians.
And as for me:
But you, the blessed one, this is your kingdom:
and make beautiful the deeds of your rule.
Therefore it was right for you.
But in faithfulness I am a king to you, that you should not begin the enmity you have made with the Sultan.
But I will not be at rest
not to you.

Diogenes, however, was angry and said:
